module: Internal ESC calibration tool: automates a 'skew stiffness' test by sweeping 13 speeds (40 to 100 km/h) and 14 steering angles (0.5° to 7°), with the cruise control and the 'esc' controller. The result is written to skewStiffnessPivot.csv and progress is sent to the UI via the 'ESCSkewStiffnessChange' hook.
notes: States: Idling, Initialization (measures the maximum wheel angle by steering fully 2 x 2 s), Starting, Settling (waits for the target speed via cruiseControl.hasReachedTargetSpeed then esc.calibrationSettled), Measuring (waits for esc.calibrationMeasurementReady), Increasing Angle / Increasing Speed, Finished (writes the CSV, cuts the cruise control, restores normal physics speed).

Depends on the 'esc' controller (fields wheelAngleFront, pauseESCAction, doSettle, calibrationSettled, doMeasure, calibrationMeasurementReady, stiffnessFront, stiffnessRear, functions startESCCalibration/stopESCCalibration) and loads the cruiseControl extension.
During the test, be:setPhysicsSpeedFactor(1) is requested from the GE (maximum physics speed); it is reset to 0 at the end or on stop.

CSV columns: Speed,Angle,Front,Rear,Ratio,gForce, Float Angle, Test. The last two columns (floatAngle, test) are never filled in testResults and are therefore nil. The file is written to the game's working directory (relative path).
gForce = sensors.gx2 / |gravity| (gravity clamped to a minimum of 0.1). Progress in % = completed steps / (13 x 14).

onInit.desc: Initialization hook: resets all counters and results to zero, physics speed to normal and the state to Idling.

updateGFX.desc: Called every frame: advances the test state machine and drives the steering.

startSkewStiffnessTest.desc: Starts the test: gets the 'esc' controller (aborts with a log error if it does not exist), loads cruiseControl, starts the ESC calibration and switches to the Initialization state.

stopSkewStiffnessTest.desc: Stops the test: cuts the cruise control, stops the ESC calibration, restores normal physics speed and switches to the Finished state (the CSV will then be written on the next frame).
